preheader.zh: 一道改期的命令、一份写好的讲稿，和一副眼镜。
preheader.en: A rescheduled meeting, a written speech, and a pair of spectacles.

what.zh: 华盛顿讲话全文，十分钟可读完，能看到他怎样一边批评匿名信、一边承认军队的委屈。
what.en: The full speech, a ten-minute read: watch him criticise the anonymous letter while acknowledging the army's grievance.

further_reading.title: The Journals of Major Samuel Shaw (1847)

what.zh: 肖的书信与日志，第102–104页是他对纽堡会议的记述，包括眼镜一幕。
what.en: Shaw's letters and journals; pp. 102–104 give his account of the Newburgh meeting, spectacles and all.

what.zh: 英文百科条目，概述事件和匿名信作者的争议；不是一手材料。
what.en: An overview of the episode and the debate over who wrote the anonymous letters; not a primary source.

replace_reason.hook: '国会此前的答复' now evidenced as the 25 January resolves (extended D-E1); 'far from satisfactory' attributed to Shaw; '出卖大家' (stronger than 'mark for suspicion') removed; author's framing of Washington's difficulty removed from a record paragraph.
replace_reason.context: Removed unsupported '远在费城'; Shaw's account dated by its own provenance (D-E13) instead of an unverified recipient.
replace_reason.story: Speech-writing and congressman's letter now evidenced (extended D-E3, D-E4); 'trust Congress to settle accounts' evidenced (extended D-E8); interpretive sentence moved out of record paragraphs; resolution wording follows D-E9.
replace_reason.analysis: Removed '五项他没有反驳' (speech text does not support it) and the misattributed 'Shaw said he had written the speech'.
replace_reason.today: First scene duplicated the reflection's anonymous-post scenario; replaced with a 'deliver bad news yourself' scene. Second scene kept.
replace_reason.limits: '作者有争议' replaced with what the evidence says (unknown persons).

hook.zh: 前一年12月，大陆军派代表去国会递交请愿。国会委员会后来把请愿归纳为五项：发当期军饷，结算欠饷并给担保，把终身半薪折成一笔等值补偿，结算口粮和被服的亏欠。1783年1月25日，国会只答应先发一个月饷、尽快结算账目，半薪折算退回再议。在场的军官肖写道，这份答复“远不能令人满意”，只是和平已近，部队才暂时安静。
hook.en: The previous December the Continental Army had sent delegates to Congress with an address and petition. A congressional committee later summed it up in five articles: present pay; settlement of arrears with security for what was owed; commuting the promised half pay for life into a lump sum; and settling what was owed for rations and clothing. On 25 January 1783 Congress resolved only that the army would get one month's pay and that accounts would be settled as soon as possible; the half-pay commutation was sent back to committee. Major Samuel Shaw, an officer in the camp, wrote that this was "far from being satisfactory", but the certainty of peace kept the army quiet.

hook.zh: 就在这时，一封匿名信在营中传开，号召军官们集会。华盛顿以3月11日的命令把会期定在15日，结果又引出了第二封匿名信。
hook.en: Then an anonymous address began to circulate, calling the officers to a meeting. Washington, by an order of 11 March, set the meeting for the 15th instead, which drew a second anonymous address.

context.zh: 地点是纽约州纽堡的大陆军营地，独立战争已近尾声。主角是总司令华盛顿和一群服役多年的军官；3月15日的会议由盖茨少将主持。现场细节主要来自肖1783年4月的一封信，收在1847年出版的《肖日志》里。
context.en: The place was the Continental Army's camp at Newburgh, New York, with the War of Independence nearly over. The people were the commander-in-chief, George Washington, and officers who had served for years; the meeting of 15 March was chaired by Major General Horatio Gates. The details of the scene come mainly from a letter Shaw wrote in April 1783, printed in his journals in 1847.

story.zh: 肖记下了华盛顿的开场：他先为自己到场致歉，说发布开会命令时本无此意；可匿名文字传得太广，他觉得必须向军队说明自己对这些文字的看法，于是借这个机会，并为了说得更清楚，事先把想法写了下来，请大家允许他照稿宣读。
story.en: Shaw recorded how Washington began. He apologised for appearing at all: that had been no part of his intention when he issued the order. But the anonymous papers had been circulated so busily that he felt he had to give the army his view of them, and to do it clearly he had "committed his thoughts to writing", which he asked leave to read.

story.zh: 讲稿第一句就点题：“有人用一份匿名的召集，试图把你们聚到一起。”他说，匿名信的作者文笔值得称道，可惜心术不正：谁主张克制、主张再忍耐一些，谁不按他的想法行事，就被他标为可疑。
story.en: The address opened bluntly: "By an anonymous summons, an attempt has been made to convene you together." The author of the anonymous address, he said, deserved credit for the goodness of his pen, but should have had the charity not "to mark for suspicion the man who should recommend moderation and longer forbearance".

story.zh: 他请军官们不要采取任何冷静下来看会“降低你们的尊严、玷污你们一向保持的荣誉”的举动，要相信国家许下的信义，相信国会会在军队解散之前把账目公平结清。
story.en: He asked the officers not to take any step which, viewed calmly, "will lessen the dignity, and sully the glory you have hitherto maintained", and to rely on "the plighted faith of your country" and on Congress to settle their accounts fairly before the army was disbanded.

story.zh: 讲完后，他说要念一位国会议员的来信，作为国会善待军队的佐证。读完第一段，他停了一下，取出眼镜，请大家包涵他戴上，并说自己为他们效力，头发已经白了，如今眼睛也快看不见了。肖写道，这一下如此自然、毫不做作，胜过最用心的演说，在场的人眼眶都湿了。要注意：这是肖的间接转述，不是逐字原话。
story.en: After the address he said he would read a letter from "a worthy member of that body", a congressman who had always been the army's friend, as evidence of Congress's goodwill. After the first paragraph he paused, took out his spectacles and asked their indulgence while he put them on, "observing at the same time, that he had grown gray in their service, and now found himself growing blind". Shaw thought it "superior to the most studied oratory". Note that this is Shaw's report of what Washington said, not his exact words.

story.zh: 华盛顿随即离场。会议在盖茨主持下一致通过决议：军官们“以憎恶看待、以轻蔑拒绝”那封匿名信中可耻的提议，并愤慨谴责有人暗中召集军官、完全破坏纪律与秩序的企图。一周后的3月22日，国会决议：在役并服役到战争结束的军官，可领五年全薪，付现金或年息六厘的证券，代替原先承诺的终身半薪。
story.en: Washington then left. With Gates presiding, the meeting resolved unanimously that the officers "view with abhorrence, and reject with disdain, the infamous propositions contained in a late anonymous address", and condemned the secret attempt to assemble them as subversive of all discipline. A week later, on 22 March, Congress resolved that officers serving to the end of the war would receive five years' full pay, in money or in securities at six per cent interest, instead of the half pay for life they had been promised.

analysis.zh: 一种解释是（作者推断）：华盛顿把“要什么”和“怎么要”分开了。他没有说军官们的不满没有道理，而是请他们相信国会会结账；他反对的是匿名召集，以及把主张克制的人标为可疑。他本不打算到场，最后决定亲自去、照稿讲——按肖的转述，原因是匿名文字传得太广。
analysis.en: One interpretation, the author's, is that Washington separated what the officers wanted from how they were going about it. He did not say their grievance was baseless; he asked them to trust Congress to settle accounts. What he opposed was the anonymous summons and the branding of moderates as suspect. He had not meant to attend; by Shaw's account, he decided to come and read a prepared text because the anonymous papers had spread so widely.

analysis.zh: 眼镜一幕为什么有效，肖的说法是“自然、不做作”。但我们只有肖的转述，核对不了华盛顿的原话和语气。3月22日的国会决议紧跟在这次会议之后，两者有没有因果关系，现有材料说不清。
analysis.en: Why the spectacles moment worked, Shaw put down to its being natural and unaffected. But we have only his report and cannot check Washington's words or tone. The congressional resolution of 22 March followed hard on the meeting; whether one caused the other, the material we have cannot say.

today.zh: 一个团队得知年终奖要延后发放。负责人可以等传言先到，也可以自己先开口：说清楚确定的部分（会发、大约延后多久、为什么），承认不确定的部分（具体日期还没定），并说明自己也在同一条船上。坏消息由负责人第一个说出来，比让大家从匿名渠道拼凑出来，少很多猜疑。
today.en: A team learns that its year-end bonus will be paid late. The manager can wait for the rumours to arrive first, or speak first: say what is certain (it will be paid, roughly how late, and why), admit what is not (the exact date is not fixed), and make clear that she is in the same position. Bad news delivered first by the person responsible breeds far less suspicion than news pieced together from anonymous channels.

today.zh: 再比如，一个社区团队的报销积压半年，私下流传"负责人不作为"。负责人可以在会上讲一件属实的自身处境，比如自己也垫付了几个月、为此推掉了别的活，不求同情，只求让大家看见成本是共同的；然后给出一个具体的时间点和比对质更省力的出口，比如下周三前把单据汇总由他统一去催。前提是这件事属实，且后面真有动作，否则就成了表演。
today.en: Or take a community team whose reimbursements have piled up for half a year, with private talk that "the lead isn't doing anything." The lead can share one true fact about their own situation — say, that they have also fronted the costs for months and turned down other work because of it. Not to win sympathy, but so people can see the cost is shared. Then give a concrete deadline and an easier exit than confrontation, for example collecting all the receipts by next Wednesday so the lead can chase the payment in one go. The condition is that this must be true and that real action follows, otherwise it becomes theatre.

limits.zh: 眼镜一幕只有肖的转述为据，流传很广的那句“原话”不在本篇材料里，别照着演，也别把它当成万能的情绪开关。匿名信出自何人，本篇材料只说是“不明身份的人”，这里不作讨论。五年全薪的证券后来兑现得怎样，本篇没有取材，不下结论。也别说“华盛顿一人挽救了共和国”：决议是与会军官一致通过的，会议由盖茨主持，国会的决议在一周之后。
limits.en: The spectacles scene rests on Shaw's report alone, and the widely quoted line attributed to Washington is not in the material used here; do not stage it, and do not treat it as an emotional switch that always works. On who wrote the anonymous letters, the sources used here speak only of unknown persons, so this article does not go into it. How the five-year pay securities were later honoured is outside the material used here. Nor should anyone say that Washington alone saved the republic: the resolution was passed unanimously by the officers, Gates chaired the meeting, and Congress acted a week later.

edits.new: 欠饷是真的，匿名信也是真的：华盛顿在纽堡站在哪里
The Grievance Was Real, and So Was the Anonymous Letter: Washington at Newburgh
1783年3月，独立战争快打完了，军官们的饷还欠着。有人用匿名信号召他们集会施压。华盛顿本不打算到场，最后还是去了。
March 1783: the war was nearly over and the officers were still unpaid. Anonymous letters called them together to press their case. Washington had not meant to attend; in the end he went.

现场细节（华盛顿本不打算到场、照稿宣读、眼镜一幕、在场者的反应）出自肖1783年4月的一封信，收在1847年的《肖日志》中，是单一来源、事后转述；收信人在本篇取用的段落中没有写明。讲话文本取自《大陆会议日志》第24卷所印版本（OCR，有讹字）并与维基文库文本对照；军官会议决议和3月22日国会决议出自同一卷。请愿五项来自国会委员会后来的报告。“前一年12月”依上下文推定为1782年。匿名信作者不明，本篇不讨论；证券后来的兑现情况未取材。
edits.reason: Rewritten: removed unverified letter recipient; added provenance.

edits.new: The details of the scene (that Washington had not meant to attend, that he read from a prepared text, the spectacles, the officers' reaction) come from a single letter Shaw wrote in April 1783, printed in his journals in 1847; it is one source, written after the event, and the passage used here does not name the recipient. The speech is taken from the printing in volume 24 of the Journals of the Continental Congress (OCR, with errors) and checked against the Wikisource text; the officers' resolution and the congressional resolution of 22 March come from the same volume. The five articles of the petition come from a later congressional committee report. "The previous December" is taken from context to mean December 1782. The authors of the anonymous letters are not identified in these sources, and the later fate of the pay securities was not researched.
